audit_findings.title: Owner earnings include the General Partner’s claim but the denominator contains only common units
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $2.1 million anchor misallocation; computed $22.4-$33.0 million of operating value, or $0.46-$0.67 per common unit, plus an unquantified bridge-cash allocation
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated OE includes earnings allocated to the General Partner, while operating value and bridge cash are divided only by common units.
audit_findings.evidence: In summary, our limited partners received 96%, and our General Partner received 4% of the net cash generated by our activities and those of the Operating Partnership during this period.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated ownership-perimeter error: 2025 consolidated net income was $57.352 million, but only $55.252 million was attributable to common unitholders. Applying the $2.1 million difference proportionately to the scenario operating values reduces value by approximately $0.46-$0.67 per unit. That is only 2.3% or less of the $29.21 market price and cannot close the $9.39 gap between the market price and the $19.82 bull value, so it does not change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every historical OE year to income attributable to common unitholders, allocate Royalty and NPI cash under their respective GP percentages, and rerun all scenarios using only common-owned OE and excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The $72.5 million cash addition may be distributable cash rather than surplus cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $72.5 million bridge addition; computed approximately $61.4 million common distribution using 48.256 million June units at $1.272943 per unit, before the GP distribution
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds a June 30 cash balance to equity value even though a substantial portion funded the August distribution before the September 6 valuation date.
audit_findings.evidence: Our partnership agreement requires that we make a quarterly distribution in an amount equal to 100% of available cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The balance-date mismatch is demonstrated, although the exact overstatement is unresolved because post-June receipts, expenses, reserves, the GP allocation and acquisition-related cash also changed cash before September 6. The computed $61.4 million common distribution alone equals about 85% of the $72.5 million bridge and $1.25 per valuation-date unit, making the adjustment large relative to scenario values and the buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June 30-to-September 6 cash rollforward showing the August common and GP distributions, operating receipts and payments, acquisition contributions, accrued obligations and permissible reserves; rerun the bridge using only common-owned excess cash remaining on September 6.

audit_findings.title: Perpetual growth may require dilution that the fixed share count ignores
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 49.091408 million fixed units, with terminal value representing 49.7% of base operating value and 50.9% of bull operating value
audit_findings.mechanism: Aggregate OE is grown through acquisition assumptions while the per-unit calculation holds the denominator fixed and omits future unit issuance and GP leakage.
audit_findings.evidence: Our unitholders will bear 100% of the dilution from issuing new common units while receiving essentially 96% of the benefit, as 4% of the benefit goes to our General Partner.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved modeling issue, not proof that future acquisitions will be dilutive. Nevertheless, DMLP has demonstrated its use of equity-funded acquisitions, including 7.757 million units issued in 2024, 0.916 million in 2025 and 0.836 million in July 2026. Because common holders bear all issuance dilution while receiving less than all incremental cash flow, aggregate acquisition growth cannot be treated automatically as growth per existing unit. The exposure reaches roughly half of base and bull operating value and is therefore reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Split each scenario into organic same-asset growth and acquisition growth, then model acquisition consideration, units issued, GP leakage and incremental common-attributable OE. Rerun value per unit using the resulting annual diluted unit counts.

audit_findings.title: Outstanding NPI capital commitments may suppress future cash flows
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $10.4 million outstanding at June 30, 2026; computed maximum common-level burden of approximately $10.0 million or $0.20 per unit before discounting
audit_findings.mechanism: Capital expenditures on NPI properties reduce future NPI payments and therefore common-unit OE when paid or charged through the NPI calculation.
audit_findings.evidence: From a cash perspective, as of December 31, 2025, the Minerals NPI had outstanding capital commitments, primarily in the Bakken region, of $8.5 million.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether these commitments were already reserved or reflected in the anchor remains unresolved, but the latest filing states that the NPI was in a surplus position. Even treating the entire $10.4 million as an incremental charge, applying the 96.97% NPI interest and 99% common allocation produces about $10.0 million, equal to roughly 1.0%-1.5% of scenario equity values and $0.20 per unit. That scale cannot change the current conclusion that the $29.21 price exceeds even the $19.82 bull value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the monthly NPI statements and capital-commitment rollforward, identify amounts already deducted or reserved, and include any remaining common-attributable charge in the explicit forecast rather than as debt.

audit_findings.title: Episodic lease and assignment proceeds remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $9.0 million of identified proceeds; computed $95.8-$141.3 million of operating value, or $1.95-$2.88 per unit, if no normalized recurring contribution is supportable
audit_findings.mechanism: Transaction-specific lease-extension and leasehold-assignment revenue increases anchor OE and is then compounded and capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in lease bonus revenue from 2024 to 2025 is primarily attributable to receipt of $3.6 million in 2025 from an extension of an existing lease, wherein the Partnership leased 243 net acres in two tracts of land in Reagan County, Texas for $15,000 per acre, and receipt of $5.4 million from an assignment of leasehold interests.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion is demonstrated: the $57.4 million anchor contains a $3.6 million lease extension and $5.4 million assignment. The proper normalized amount is unresolved because lease bonuses are part of DMLP's business but are irregular. Capitalizing the full identified $9.0 million accounts for approximately 11%-15% of reported scenario value, so the normalization decision is reasonably capable of changing valuation outputs and the buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Build a multi-year schedule of lease bonuses, assignments and settlement-type receipts, separate recurring leasing activity from exceptional transactions, select a documented normalized common-attributable amount, and rerun all scenarios from the adjusted anchor.

audit_findings.title: A growing terminal value may conflict with depletion economics
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 46.3%-50.9% of operating value; computed approximately $282.9-$458.6 million of terminal value
audit_findings.mechanism: The terminal calculation assumes 2.5% perpetual OE growth without separately charging the reserve replacement, acquisition funding, GP leakage or dilution needed to offset depletion.
audit_findings.evidence: Our oil and natural gas reserves and the underlying properties are depleting assets, and there are limitations on our ability to replace them.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved sustainability assumption rather than a demonstrated numerical error. DMLP owns substantial perpetual mineral interests and may benefit from third-party development, but its proved reserves are depleting and it distributes substantially all available cash. The record does not establish that 2.5% perpetual growth is achievable per existing unit. Because nearly half of operating value depends on the terminal calculation, a depletion-consistent terminal assumption could materially alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile forecast production to reserve decline, quantify reinvestment or acquisitions required to replace depletion, and model the associated unit issuance and GP leakage. Rerun with no-growth and declining terminal cases alongside any supported per-unit growth case.
